thought.text: Current behavior confirmed: the dot regex `[^\w\s-]` strips dots, so `api.v1` → `apiv1`. Fix is to allow dots in the character class.

reasoning_content:
Current behavior: `slugify("api.v1 endpoint")`:
- text = "api.v1 endpoint"
- lower -> "api.v1 endpoint"
- re.sub(r"[^\w\s-]", "", ...) strips the dot -> "apiv1 endpoint"
- re.sub(r"[-\s]+", "-", ...) -> "apiv1-endpoint"

We want "api.v1-endpoint". So dots should be preserved.

The task: preserve dots. Edit src/slugify.py so the regex `[^\w\s-]` allows dots. Change to `[^\w\s.-]` — but need to be careful with the `.` inside character class: inside `[...]`, `.` is literal, so `[^\w\s.-]` works. Need to place `-` at end to avoid range interpretation. `[^\w\s.-]` — the `-` is at the end, fine.

But wait: existing test `test_special_characters` asserts `slugify("Special @#$% Characters!") == "special-characters"` — dots preserved won't affect this. What about other chars? The unicode test "Café déjà vu!" contains no dots.

But should we preserve dots in a way that doesn't break "Hello World!" etc. Let's just adjust the character class to keep dots. Also consider the current test `test_basic_slugify`: "Hello World!" -> no dots. Good.

Edge: what about dots at beginning/end with strip("-")? e.g. ".hidden" -> ".hidden" stripping "-" doesn't remove dot. That's fine per the requirement.

The requirement says preserve dots. Simplest fix: change `r"[^\w\s-]"` to `r"[^\w\s.-]"` (dot literal in char class). Also maybe the second regex `[-\s]+` stays.
